solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Previously super-punctilious special near pipped

blocks.note: SP is a standard abbreviation for special
to pip someone or ice them is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: A fussy editor fusses over the word 'special' being narrowly beaten to a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previously' marks an obsolete sense: Chambers lists spiced as an old word for over-scrupulous.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage spiced described someone overnice or overscrupulous, which matches excessive punctiliousness.

clue.text: Mayday inviting in count's dull bods

indicators.note: to invite someone in is to bring them inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Mayday and SOS are both distress calls
to count up is to add

explanation.surface: A distress signal goes out from a nobleman's boring guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' reads as an aristocrat but is the verb. Bods is British slang for people.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddos is British slang for pathetic, boring people, matching dull bods.

clue.text: Sophocles' swift swing exercises excellent Teian — almost

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
ripe can mean fully developed or excellent
taken as written; a Teian is from Teos, Anacreon's city

explanation.surface: A Greek-themed line about a poet from Teos working out, almost excellently.
explanation.walkthrough: Sophocles' tragedies turn on a sudden reversal of fortune; Aristotle named it in the Poetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripeteia is the sudden reversal of fortune in Greek tragedy, the swift swing of a plot.

clue.text: Neat bloomer that perfumes pastures

blocks.note: neat is an old word for cattle
a bloomer is a mistake, as is a slip

explanation.surface: A tidy flower that scents the meadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' and 'bloomer' both pose as part of a flower picture; one is cattle and the other a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a fragrant yellow wildflower of meadows, so it is a plant that scents pastures.

clue.text: Mitsotakis's business is therefore back from oblivion

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
the final letter

explanation.surface: The Greek prime minister's work is therefore back from obscurity.
explanation.walkthrough: Mitsotakis, a Greek prime minister, stands in for Greek; ergon is Greek for work or business.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergon is the Greek word for work or a task, which is a Greek leader's business.

clue.text: Acts damn politely with those kettling demonstrators

indicators.note: kettling means hemming in from all sides, so only the letters on the edges are wanted

blocks.note: dee is a polite euphemism for damn
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Police acts of kettling protesters are condemned in polite terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Kettling is the police tactic of penning protesters inside a cordon.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeds and acts are both words for things done.

clue.text: Oregon snuck in limits for Loyalists

indicators.note: something that has snuck in has got inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: ties are restrictions or limits
OR is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Oregon

explanation.surface: Someone from Oregon slips past the boundaries to join the loyalist side.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories took their name from the faction loyal to the crown, and the word was also used for American Loyalists in the Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyalists who backed the British crown during the American Revolution were commonly called Tories.

clue.text: Sovereign Troy has a queen in Hecuba finally

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, its last letter

blocks.note: T is an abbreviation for troy weight
's is the contracted form of has
taken as written
R is for regina, queen
taken as written
the final letter

explanation.surface: Troy has a queen in Hecuba, wife of King Priam.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is pure Homer, but Troy is the weight system, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was an empress of Russia, a female sovereign.

clue.text: Variety of forbidden fruit

indicators.note: what is forbidden is not allowed in, so those letters are kept out

blocks.note: o' is a short form of of
an orange is a fruit

explanation.surface: A kind of forbidden fruit, as in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forbidden fruit' is a set phrase luring towards the apple; here forbidden acts on 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of goods is a variety or assortment of them.

clue.text: On which we watch innocent present?

blocks.note: an innocent can mean a simpleton or idiot
a Christmas box is a present

explanation.surface: A question about what an innocent bystander might be watching.
explanation.walkthrough: Idiot box is slang for the television set.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiot box is a slang name for television, the set people watch programmes on.

clue.text: Being inclined to swinging, wife is caught in fling

indicators.note: things caught in another are trapped inside it

blocks.note: to shy is to fling or throw
W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife with a taste for partner-swapping gets caught in an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fling' reads as an affair, but it is the verb throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Swishy describes something that swishes, inclined to swing or sweep with a rustling motion.

clue.text: Augur is mostly rustic who'd a changing form

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
letters changing their form are rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: forest as an adjective means sylvan or rustic
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A country soothsayer who used to look different is predicting the future.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur and to foreshadow both mean to give an advance sign of something coming.

clue.text: Woman in newspaper in costly coupling?

indicators.note: the first in places one item inside the next
the second in places the combined item inside the outer word

blocks.note: dear means expensive
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
W is the abbreviation for woman

explanation.surface: A female journalist appears in a tabloid story about an expensive marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a mechanical sense of coupling, not a romantic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Draw-gear is the coupling apparatus by which railway carriages are hitched together and pulled.

clue.text: Engineering and science radiate a glowing warmth

indicators.note: engineering means building something by design, so the letters are constructed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Engineering and science give off a warm glow of achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: To incandesce is to glow with heat, giving off light and warmth.

clue.text: Sponge divers tire?

blocks.note: a diver is old slang for a pickpocket, as is a dip
a tyre (tire) is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A sponge diver wonders whether all that plunging is tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' looks like the sea creature divers collect, but it is a heavy drinker. The question mark flags the loose leap from tire to the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is slang for a heavy drinker, and dipso is short for dipsomaniac, an alcoholic.

clue.text: Intimidating women's doctor struggles

blocks.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
agon is a Greek word for a contest or struggle

explanation.surface: A doctor treating women who find things a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a fierce, intimidating woman, often a formidable older one.

clue.text: Open option in vers libre (except Irish or the equivalent)

indicators.note: except shuts one piece out, and the bracketed alternative stands in its place

blocks.note: vers libre is French for free verse
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language
OTE is short for 'or the equivalent'

explanation.surface: An open form of poetry, with or without Irish features.
explanation.definitionFit: A free vote is one where members may vote as they choose, not along party lines, an open option.

clue.text: Lift up sauce boat

indicators.note: to lift a thing is to take it away, so the named letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written
ketchup is a tomato sauce

explanation.surface: Someone lifts the gravy boat to pour the sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift up' reads as one verb, but 'Lift' is the instruction and 'up' the letters it removes from the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel, so it is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Perhaps philosopher's stone is fine and acceptable

blocks.note: 's is the contracted form of is
an eric was a blood-fine paid in old Irish law
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: Someone judges a philosopher's gravestone fine and acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone' tempts as the S for stone, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sericon was an alchemists' name for a red tincture, one candidate substance for the philosopher's stone, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Heavy South African men nailing notoriously cruel despot

indicators.note: nailing a thing means pinning it in place, gripped between the outer letters

blocks.note: ou is South African slang for a man; plural ous
Nero was the notoriously cruel Roman emperor

explanation.surface: South Africans catch a brutal tyrant in a heavy-handed operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous means burdensome, which is one sense of heavy, as in a heavy responsibility.

clue.text: Millions invested in auctioning site — it was steep

definitions.note: 'it was' marks an obsolete sense of the verb

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: eBay is the online auction site
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: Millions were poured into an auction website, and its prices were steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' reads as an adjective for high prices but is the old verb meaning to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: Embay is an old Spenserian verb meaning to bathe or soak, which is to steep.

clue.text: Viewpoint echoed in speech that offers an alternative

indicators.note: in speech means as said out loud, so the word's sound is what counts

blocks.note: to echo something is to mirror it
or is the word that offers an alternative

explanation.surface: A viewpoint echoed in a speech that offers a different option.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirador is a watchtower or belvedere with a view, so it is a viewpoint.

clue.text: Paddy's bowled over with second flight

indicators.note: something bowled over is knocked onto its back, so the word is turned round

blocks.note: a paddy is a fit of temper, as is a pet; read as plural
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An Irishman is knocked down by a second blow.
explanation.walkthrough: A paddy and a pet are both British words for a sulk or fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a run of steps.

clue.text: Small chap's title showering respect on frequenter of SW1?

blocks.note: Shri is an Indian honorific title of respect
SW1 is the Westminster postcode, home of Parliament, which MPs frequent

explanation.surface: A short man's title honours a Westminster regular.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the London postal district containing the Houses of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrimp is a dismissive slang word for a small person.

clue.text: Vehicle pulling out pinks and races

indicators.note: pulling something out of a word removes it

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
pinks are a kind of carnation

explanation.surface: A vehicle pulls out of a race course decorated with pink flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'races' suggests motor racing alongside the vehicle, but it means peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in the sense of a people of common descent overlaps with nation as a word for a people.

clue.text: Nuts lasted as they're ____

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nuts keep longer because they have been treated with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is filled by the answer: read as a whole, the clue says the nuts kept because they were preserved, while 'Nuts' also mixes up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Salting preserves food, so salted nuts last longer, which the completed sentence describes.

clue.text: Underworld goddess grabbing last of these small stilettos?

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only
grabbing something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Hel is the Norse goddess of the underworld
the final letter
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A goddess of the dead snatches a pair of small stilettos.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows stilettos is a definition by example: they are one kind of heel, not the only kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilettos are thin high heels, so they are an example of heels on shoes.

clue.text: I'm unlikely to get out rifle which has been discharged

indicators.note: a gun discharged has gone off, so the letters are blown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner who fired a gun reflects that release is unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharged' tempts as release from prison, which the definition denies.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence, who is unlikely ever to be released.

clue.text: Informally go trapping a lieutenant — go easy

indicators.note: something trapping another holds it inside

blocks.note: waz is British slang for urinating, informally to go
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: Someone casually tells a lieutenant to take it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' appears twice: the first is slang for urinating, the second part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To waltz through something is to do it easily, to go with no effort.

clue.text: Beet is British and low in calories

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
lite is the marketing spelling of light, low in calories

explanation.surface: British beetroot is a low-calorie food.
explanation.definitionFit: Blite is a name for plants of the goosefoot family, including strawberry blite, related to beet.

clue.text: Newly appointed I arrive in warm seaside area

indicators.note: newly appointed suggests things freshly set out, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new appointee arrives at a sunny resort by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the warm Mediterranean coastline of France and Italy, a resort area by the sea.

clue.text: Tag left next on murderee

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Abel was murdered by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: A toe tag is attached next to a murder victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag and a label are both small attached tickets giving identifying information.

clue.text: Scots lawyer's stay sheltering rank diagnostician?

indicators.note: something sheltering another holds it inside, giving cover around it

blocks.note: in Scots law a sist is a stay of proceedings
olid means rank or foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A Scottish lawyer's adjournment protects a high-ranking medical expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a position in a hierarchy, but it means smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A solidist held the old medical theory that disease arises from the solid parts of the body, a diagnostic view, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Freedom of speech is given by this energy only found in punk

definitions.text: Freedom of speech is given by this

indicators.note: pieces found in another are located inside it

blocks.note: punk and mutton are both old slang for a prostitute
E is the symbol for energy
but means only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A punk anthem about free speech, delivered with nothing but energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freedom of speech' is read wryly: the button gives freedom from speech, not the right to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mute button silences a device, granting relief from talk, a playful twist on the civil liberty.

clue.text: Sprite gambolling in some ferns

indicators.note: gambolling means leaping about playfully, so the letters jump into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fairy frolics among the ferns.
explanation.definitionFit: Pteris is a genus of ferns, the brakes, so it names a group of fern species.

clue.text: 'Ercules, eg, in closing letter is set to love

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: zed is the last letter of the alphabet
Hercules is an example of a hero; with the H dropped, as the apostrophe in the name shows, hero loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch hero of myth ends up in love.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Ercules tells the solver to drop the H from the word for which he is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Love means nil in tennis, so a scoreboard set to love has been reset to nothing.
